forma.author: Forma contributors
forma.method: Original editorial capability records written from the components, demonstrations and contracts in this package.
forma.scope: A curated pattern library for choosing the next implementation step, not a catalog of external websites.
limits: No third-party catalog records, aesthetic scores, screenshots or website assets are included.
Authorship of the editorial records does not imply invention of UX theory, observed mechanisms, standards or dependencies described by their linked resources.
An entry identifies available code, a runnable demo or an implementation contract; it is not evidence of a working integration in the destination project.

entries.name: Quiet workspace shell
entries.idea: A stable navigation edge and a separate working surface let product content carry the visual emphasis.
entries.whenToUse: An operational app needs a reusable starting point for its navigation, toolbar and content without changing its routes.
structure: Keep navigation, work area and contextual actions in separate regions.
Use repeated insets to align the toolbar and content; allow the content track to shrink.
adapt: Start from the scoped shell CSS and demo behavior, then attach real data and routes.
Choose density from the actual list or form, rather than scaling the whole screen.
avoid: Do not treat the demo's in-memory state as production persistence.
The simple demo toggle is not the complete lighting editor.
verify: Navigate by keyboard and verify the selected route after returning.
Use long labels and a narrow viewport to check content clipping and action reachability.

limits: The demo uses in-memory data. Consumer routing, persistence and integration remain separate work.
This catalog record supplies no fresh browser capture.

entries.name: Editable identity card
entries.idea: A preview can look like a physical object while profile editing remains a small, explicit transaction.
entries.whenToUse: The product needs a profile card and editable identity fields that agree before and after saving.
structure: Pair a card preview with the fields that actually belong to the account.
Separate the working draft, the persisted identity and a visual variation.
adapt: Use the destination project's membership and role model; omit unsupported fields.
Keep copy, export and appearance variation as separate commands with their own outcomes.
avoid: Do not invent a membership tier to fill a decorative badge.
Do not report an exported card when only the preview changed.
verify: Change a name, cancel, reopen and confirm the saved identity is unchanged.
Save a valid edit and verify both the preview and persisted fields after reopening.

limits: A ready-to-use profile card component is not bundled. Export, persistence and material rendering must be implemented in the destination project.

entries.name: Preferences with a visible commit boundary
entries.idea: Settings become predictable when each preference says whether it previews immediately or changes only after confirmation.
entries.whenToUse: Preferences span profile, appearance, data or account tasks and need coherent navigation and save behavior.
structure: Group controls by the decision a person is making, not by equal card sizes.
Keep body scrolling separate from reachable confirmation actions.
adapt: State which values are immediate and which belong to a draft.
Use tabs or another navigation pattern suited to the number of groups and the length of their labels.
avoid: Do not create empty product areas to match a reference screenshot.
Do not let changing tabs silently commit a draft unless the contract explicitly says so.
verify: Exercise preview, save, cancel, reset and reopen with changed values.
Check focus, long help text and the last control while the virtual keyboard reduces available height.

limits: This record describes an implementation contract; it does not include a working integration or a new rendered test.

entries.name: Contextual light-pool editor
entries.idea: A light-pool editor separates group positioning, local positioning with Alt and relative distance, while selection, color, intensity and grain retain independent state.
entries.whenToUse: An approved appearance mechanism needs movable lights and per-context persistence, rather than a static palette.
structure: Anchor the editor to the declared working region and keep its preview bounds stable.
Dragging a pool's center normally translates every pool by the selected pool's delta; holding Alt when pointerdown occurs moves only the selected pool.
The distance ring keeps its selected anchor fixed and scales the other radial vectors; it is not a position control.
adapt: Mount the supplied AppearanceEditor with scoped styles, then connect preview, confirmed save, cancel and contextual color to the destination owners. The lab demonstrates local storage only.
Use the portable profile for the initial two pools, third-pool insertion and selection; adding or choosing a pool does not redistribute existing coordinates.

Clamp the selected pointer target to the stage, then apply the same model delta to the other pools. Paint actual coordinates and clip offstage points; do not clamp the group or pin visual substitutes to the edge.
Preserve finite offstage coordinates when saving and reopening. Color, mode and selection changes do not move any pool.
For a selected anchor outside the stage, keep positive radial scaling and clip the painting; a negative stage edge-fit must not reverse or amplify the vectors.
avoid: Do not make ordinary center drag local-only or make Alt drag translate the group.
Do not change the model or apparent relative vectors merely to keep all lights visible.
Do not replace the agreed anchored panel with a blocking full-screen modal.
verify: Add the third pool without moving the previous two, then compare every pool during default drag, Alt drag and ring adjustment as three separate operations.

Replay gestures.thirdDragFixture from the portable profile: after adding the third pool with +, drag the selected pool at index 1 to normalized coordinates [0.85,0.8]; expected model coordinates in array order are [[120.5,165],[116.5,107],[124.5,223]]. The selected point stays inside while the other two are clipped, with no edge proxies.

During a default drag, preserve relative vectors within the model's quantization tolerance; during an Alt drag, keep the other pools unchanged; during a ring adjustment, keep the anchor fixed and check radial scaling.
Save and reopen in light and dark modes; confirm offstage coordinates, context, color, grain and intensity independently.

limits: The original vanilla module and styles are executable; framework adapters, production persistence and contextual data still belong to the consumer.
The compact profile is an independent fidelity contract. This record supplies no fresh capture or proof that every destination measurement matches it.
The profile records an approved observed mechanism; this editorial entry does not claim that Forma invented the appearance or interaction.

entries.name: BookObject: closed volume and readable surfaces
entries.idea: The cover, binding and page block must form a continuous volume before material polish can make the book convincing.
entries.whenToUse: A three-dimensional book must rotate while preserving legibility, thickness and material cues beyond its front view.
structure: Treat front, back, binding and pages as coordinated geometry with declared dimensions.
Keep artwork, material response, camera pose and input behavior independently adjustable.
adapt: Use BookObject with the consumer-supplied Three.js loader for volume rendering.
Reuse the mechanism but set content, identity and adaptation requirements from the destination.
avoid: Do not hide a binding gap with a shadow or choose only a flattering angle.
A tilted flat image is not equivalent to the requested volume.
verify: Inspect front, binding, back, page edges and grazing angles for gaps and intersections.
Compare emboss depth, foil response and text under fixed camera and lighting; verify reduced motion and fallback.

limits: The consumer supplies Three.js when selecting WebGL volume rendering.
The geometry helper is reusable code; each new object and visual target needs its own validation.

entries.name: PassportObject: articulated cover and turning page
entries.idea: A hinged cover, page block and turning leaf share attached roots while their opening, materials and orientation remain independently adjustable.
entries.whenToUse: The destination needs a portable articulated object and accepts a simplified Three mechanism with its own validation, rather than requiring parity with an existing approved CSS passport.
structure: Separate the rotating assembly from the centered model so back and open views remain framed.
Keep the cover hinge and turning leaf attached, limit page turning by cover opening, and retain a labeled static fallback.
adapt: Mount the supplied PassportObject and scoped CSS with the original BookObject cover painter and the destination's explicit Three loader.
Connect content, opening, page turning, material and fit to the actual consumer; keep complete identity text and actions accessible in its DOM.
Preserve an already approved CSS passport when that exact mechanism or visual result is required; this Three module is a separate implementation.
avoid: Do not treat a static fallback or geometry-only tests as working articulated rendering.
Do not claim the historical CSS passport's wrapping leather, end caps, physical simulation or visual approval for this simplified object.
Do not treat CPU render submission time as GPU utilization or a physical-device benchmark.
verify: Observe actual WebGL output while opening the cover, turning the page and rotating front/back views at narrow and wide sizes.
Check the full open envelope, long content, live reduced motion, loader/context failure and repeated disposal/remount.
Keep input/range controls synchronized with keyboard changes; test restoration separately from a full reload.

limits: Executable original Three adaptation with explicit dependencies; no current consumer or browser capture is certified by this catalog record.
This is separate from the approved CSS passport and does not inherit its geometry, material, content or visual acceptance.
The material-profile identity-card record remains an implementation contract; this component does not supply its account backend or editing workflow.

entries.name: Relationships before graph layout
entries.idea: A useful graph keeps the source relationship stable while camera, projection and selection change around it.
entries.whenToUse: People need to follow real links or inspect a related subset of notes, documents or entities.
structure: Separate occurrences, resolved destinations, projected edges, positions and camera state.
Offer a readable relation list alongside the spatial view.
adapt: Choose direction, multiplicity and grouping semantics before selecting a renderer.
Retain origin and revision when a relation is inferred or derived.
avoid: Do not invent links merely because nodes sit near one another.
Do not convert a visual connection into a confirmed semantic fact.
verify: Follow a relation to its exact source and distinguish repeated occurrences from unique documents.
Change filters and zoom, then recover the view without changing the data.

limits: No graph engine, indexing service or consumer dataset is supplied by this record.

entries.name: Colors assigned by responsibility
entries.idea: Brand, selection, semantic state, data series and ambient color can coexist without inheriting one another's meanings.
entries.whenToUse: A palette looks coherent in isolation but becomes ambiguous or unreadable when actual states are combined.
structure: Map colors to roles and contexts before editing numeric values.
Compare the final composed background, not just isolated token pairs.
adapt: Preserve approved brand colors and adjust the role or surrounding surface when possible.
Use the color helper only where its object palette fits the agreed artifact.
avoid: Do not prohibit a hue or gradient as a universal rule.
Do not treat a successful two-color contrast calculation as a translucent-background audit.
verify: Check selection, error and a colored data series together in every supported theme.
Observe text and focus on the final gradient or material, including hover and disabled states.

limits: The color helper is executable; the destination token system is not generated automatically.
Some object palette parameters come from documented observation; authorship of this record does not erase their provenance.

entries.name: Motion with an interruption contract
entries.idea: An animation is a state transition that must remain understandable when reversed, interrupted or disabled.
entries.whenToUse: Movement should explain feedback, spatial continuity or a specific progression through content.
structure: Declare trigger, start, intermediate states, completion and interruption.
Keep important content readable when the animation never initializes.
adapt: Use the current stack and the simplest mechanism that meets the interaction requirements.
Define a reduced-motion alternative that preserves information and actions.
avoid: Do not add animated sections to satisfy a quota.
Do not hide content permanently when an observer or animation library fails.
verify: Interrupt and reverse the sequence at several points rather than testing only its endpoint.
Confirm static content and action availability under reduced motion and failed initialization.

limits: This record describes an implementation contract; it does not include a working integration or a new rendered test.

entries.name: One owner for each space
entries.idea: Spacing is easier to refine when each distance belongs to one container and expresses one relationship.
entries.whenToUse: Content appears off-center, crowded or disconnected despite apparently consistent spacing values.
structure: Identify the available region, reading column, groups and control boundaries.
Assign insets to the container and repeated spacing between siblings to its layout rule.
adapt: Measure the intended alignment reference before choosing flex, grid or auto margins.
Let content pressure determine wrapping and stacking; reuse the existing spacing scale.
avoid: Do not combine parent gap with child margins for the same distance.
Do not center panel content against the whole viewport when a sidebar reduces its working region.
verify: Compare header, body and footer insets and the declared container center.
Use long labels and multiline errors to confirm that within-group spacing stays distinguishable from between-group spacing.

limits: This record describes an implementation contract; it does not include a working integration or a new rendered test.

entries.name: Type tested with the content it carries
entries.idea: A typographic hierarchy works only when the loaded font, real language and available width support its intended roles.
entries.whenToUse: Text hierarchy, numeric comparison or localization needs refinement while preserving the product's identity.
structure: Separate reading text, headings, control labels and comparable numeric values.
Choose line length and leading together with the real font metrics.
adapt: Start with the existing family and available weights; add a family only for a clear function.
Check language coverage, fallback and licensing before relying on a typeface.
avoid: Do not shrink essential text to conceal a layout overflow.
Do not assume that declaring a font family means the font loaded.
verify: Render accents, descenders, long words, large numbers and the supported languages.
Test zoom or text scaling and compare numeric alignment without losing units.

entries.name: Forms that preserve the draft
entries.idea: Validation should help complete the current transaction without discarding already-correct work.
entries.whenToUse: A form needs predictable submission, clear asynchronous errors and recovery after a partial failure.
structure: Keep label, control, help and error in one perceptual group.
Model editing, submission, success, failure and unknown outcome separately.
adapt: Use existing controls and server error codes; associate errors with stable field identities.
Preserve the draft while allowing the user to correct only the affected values.
avoid: Do not clear valid fields after a failed request.
Do not move focus on every validation keystroke or rely on color alone.
verify: Submit invalid input, fix the named field with a keyboard and confirm a valid result.
Simulate a delayed response and an expired session while retaining permitted draft data.

entries.name: Search with explicit scope and stale-result control
entries.idea: A result belongs to a query, scope and revision; changing any of them must not let an old response repaint the current search.
entries.whenToUse: A product combines text, tags, colors, recent queries or a command palette over changing content.
structure: Declare the search scope, fields, filter semantics, ranking and result completeness.
Separate typed text, applied query, pending request and accepted response.
adapt: Normalize text according to the product language and display active filters.
Use request identity and revision checks in addition to debouncing.
avoid: Do not call substring matching semantic search.
Do not use the theme accent as evidence that an item matches a content-color filter.
verify: Start query A, change scope and issue B, then deliver A last; only B may update the current results.
Exercise empty, partial, unavailable and no-match states with keyboard dismissal and focus return.

limits: This record describes an implementation contract; it does not include a working integration or a new rendered test.

entries.name: A chart and its explanation share one dataset
entries.idea: Values, marks, labels and accompanying copy should be different views of the same identified calculation.
entries.whenToUse: A dashboard needs readable comparison and honest interpretation of missing, delayed or rounded data.
structure: Declare the question, unit, range, series identity and data revision.
Keep annotations, the legend and the accessible alternative tied to the same metric.
adapt: Choose a chart from the comparison being made, not the visual style of the page.
Keep authoritative domain calculations and explain the display rounding policy.
avoid: Do not replace missing data with zero to complete a line.
Do not infer causality or a semantic relationship from proximity in a chart.
verify: Reconcile displayed totals, labels and prose against the authoritative input.
Test negative, zero, missing and extreme values, plus keyboard access to the underlying information.

entries.name: List and detail keep one selection
entries.idea: Width changes can alter the arrangement of a list and its detail view without losing the user's place in the task.
entries.whenToUse: The same product must support one-region mobile navigation and side-by-side work at larger widths.

Define the return path before collapsing the two regions into one.
adapt: Use measured content pressure to select a layout breakpoint.
Preserve filter, selection and scroll position according to the navigation contract.
avoid: Do not clear the selected item when a device rotates or a window resizes.
Do not count a phone-shaped desktop preview as device testing.
verify: Open a detail view, narrow and widen the viewport, then return to the same filtered list.
Check text scaling, virtual keyboard, removed items and direct links.

entries.name: A landing page built from available evidence

entries.whenToUse: A new marketing page needs a message, credible supporting material and a real next step.
structure: Connect the visitor's question to a supported claim, available material and an action.
Choose the reading sequence from that decision, then set the visual hierarchy.
adapt: Use the brand's actual vocabulary, images and verified conditions.
Label demonstration data and distinguish a proposal from an existing product feature.
avoid: Do not invent testimonials, usage metrics or prices to populate a layout.
Do not remove required information merely to make the page look minimal.
verify: Trace each material claim to its source and inspect the page with its real content.
Follow the primary action to the intended destination and check the reading order at narrow widths.

entries.name: Character identity before surface polish
entries.idea: A character remains recognizable through changes of medium when its proportions, negative spaces and expression have an explicit identity contract.
entries.whenToUse: An existing mascot needs improved rendering or adaptation between flat artwork and a 3D model.
structure: Record the silhouette, facial landmarks, negative spaces and characteristic gesture.
Separate identity-preserving geometry from lighting and surface finish.
adapt: Use authorized character assets and match the requested editable format.
Evaluate small-scale recognition before adding texture or secondary motion.
avoid: Do not change the face to hide a material or lighting problem.
Do not claim a flattened image is a rigged or editable character model.
verify: Compare the same pose at useful output sizes and from the required viewpoints.
Check face readability and edge quality against the actual delivery backgrounds.

entries.name: Export that preserves the promised layers
entries.idea: The delivered file must preserve the content and editability promised by the preview, with losses identified per layer.
entries.whenToUse: A design becomes a document, presentation, image or other file that will be opened in another tool.
structure: Name the authoring source, preview format, delivery format and expected editor.
Track required text, relationships, dimensions and layer capabilities independently.
adapt: Reuse the existing export path and preserve the editable source.
Inspect the exported result in the destination tool rather than relying on a download toast.
avoid: Do not describe a rasterized slide as containing editable text.
Do not treat a PNG extension or visible checkerboard as proof of transparency.
verify: Reopen the delivered file and compare content count, order, typography and dimensions.
Test promised editing, alpha edges and round-trip properties with an independent source.

entries.name: Fidelity as independent measurements
entries.idea: A reproduction is testable when the expected state is captured independently and each difference has a defined comparison rule.
entries.whenToUse: An approved mechanism is being transferred or a visually similar result keeps behaving differently.
structure: Fix the source revision, comparable state and dimensions before editing the target.
Separate geometry, behavior, material and output claims instead of hiding them inside one score.
adapt: Use the portable fidelity checker for the measurements it supports.
Link observed evidence to the actual loaded target files and relevant interaction.
avoid: Do not derive expected values from the implementation being tested.
Do not widen tolerances merely to turn a failure green.
verify: Run a discriminating interaction, not only an initial-state screenshot.
Verify that missing measurements and unknown revisions prevent a claim of complete parity.

limits: The package includes scripts/check_fidelity.py, but the consumer must provide independent observations.
The checker validates declared measurements; it cannot authenticate the meaning of captured pixels.

entries.name: Inspect the served result, then fix one cause
entries.idea: An implementation is reviewed in the state people can actually use, while static checks remain a separate source of evidence.
entries.whenToUse: A change passes tests but still looks wrong, clips content or fails during interaction.
structure: Record the loaded revision, viewport, device scale, state and fonts before comparison.
Inspect overall organization, then isolate the responsible spatial, content or material difference.
adapt: Keep before and after captures under comparable conditions.
Select the smallest correction that addresses the observed cause and rerun affected states.
avoid: Do not declare visual approval from a syntax or geometry test.
Do not report a stale browser page as the newly delivered version.
verify: Confirm the actual resource identity and revisit the changed interaction.
Check focus, overflow, extreme content and supported themes in the requested viewport range.

entries.name: Selected media with a traceable receipt
entries.idea: A media selection carries its author, source, stated license and file identity into the delivered project.
entries.whenToUse: The project lacks an authorized image or video, and a relevant asset from a media collection would serve the content.
structure: Search first, inspect candidates, then download only the asset identified by the selected manifest ID.
Keep the credit receipt with the file and propagate required attribution into the final artifact.
adapt: Use the Forma media helper and the smallest relevant provider query.
Confirm the intended use and rights on the source page before publication.
avoid: Do not present stock material as the actual team, product or customer.
Do not treat a provider's license metadata as proof that all rights involving depicted people or trademarks are cleared.
